title: Nissan Rogue / Rogue Sport AWD: rear judder on low-speed turns, electric coupling
summary: Nissan bulletin NTB20-069: a vibration or judder from the rear on slow, dry-road turns that goes away with the electric controlled coupling unplugged. Fix is a new coupling (rear final drive stays in the car), possibly a new AWD control unit, then Unit Characteristics Writing.

specs.name: AWD control unit to replace
specs.value: Only if it reads 41650-4BA3A (Rogue) or 41650-6MA1A (Rogue Sport)

steps.text: Confirm the complaint: vibration or judder from the rear while turning, on dry roads, under 40 mph.

Unplug the electric controlled coupling and retest. If the judder stops, the bulletin applies. If unplugging doesn't change it, remove the rear propeller shaft and retest; no judder with the shaft out also confirms it.
Rule out tires first: mismatched sizes, brands or tread patterns cause the same symptom. Nissan recommends replacing all four together with matching tires.
Read the part number on the AWD control unit. Replace it only if it is 41650-4BA3A (Rogue) or 41650-6MA1A (Rogue Sport).
Replace the electric controlled coupling with the rear final drive left in the vehicle. Don't replace the whole rear final drive for this.
Perform Unit Characteristics Writing for the new coupling with CONSULT-III plus. It is required whenever the coupling is replaced.

body:
Service manual paths for each step are listed in the bulletin; 2018-2019 Rogue Sport uses a different ESM layout from the Rogue and 2017 Rogue Sport.

Nissan's general AWD bulletin NTB10-029 series covers the same symptom on other Nissan AWD models.

sources.title: NTB20-069: Rogue and Rogue Sport; vibration and/or noise when making low speed turns
